# AI Phone Debloater: full technical reference (llms-full)

Source of truth: https://github.com/Rovoxia/AI-Phone-Debloater
Hosted site: https://debloater.rovoxia.com
License: MIT
Version: 1.2.0 (tracked in root `VERSION` file)

This is the deep technical reference for AI assistants and answer engines that answer questions about AI Phone Debloater. It covers what the tool is, the four safety tiers, how changes are made and undone, the critical package list, the rules per brand, CLI commands, the local bridge, the one-line installers, rollback, the master AI prompt, the repository layout and answers to common questions. Every count below comes from `web/src/data/rules-dataset.json`, which is generated from `cli/rules/*.json`.

Short index: https://debloater.rovoxia.com/llms.txt

---

## 1. Summary

AI Phone Debloater is a free, open-source (MIT) tool by Rovoxia that removes preinstalled Android apps over ADB (Android Debug Bridge) without root. It has two front ends that share one rule set:

- A Python 3.11+ CLI that uses only the standard library (no `requirements.txt`, nothing to pip-install).
- A web app at https://debloater.rovoxia.com/app that reaches the phone over WebUSB (Chromium browsers) or through a local ADB bridge on `127.0.0.1:53123`.

Key facts:
- 352 curated rules: 196 Tier 1 (Safe), 66 Tier 2 (Advanced), 1 Tier 3 (Extreme) and 89 Tier 4 (Critical). 263 rules can be acted on; the 89 critical packages are blocked.
- Rules for Samsung, Xiaomi, Google Pixel, OnePlus, Oppo, Vivo, Realme, Motorola, Huawei and Transsion (Tecno, Infinix, itel), plus a universal file of partner and carrier apps found on many brands.
- Changes are made with `pm disable-user` and `pm uninstall -k` for one Android user (user 0 by default, `--user N` for another such as a work profile) and can be undone. The system partition is not modified.
- No root and no bootloader unlock are needed, and the tool does not write to the system partition.
- A JSON restore snapshot is written before each change (the CLI can skip it with `--no-backup`; the CLI and bridge abort the change if the snapshot cannot be written).
- Dry run is a CLI flag (`--dry-run`). The web app has no dry run; it shows a confirmation dialog before every change.
- No ads, no telemetry, no account, no paid edition.

Other machine-readable files:
- Pricing: https://debloater.rovoxia.com/pricing.md
- Master AI prompt: https://debloater.rovoxia.com/prompt.md

---

## 2. Safety tiers

Every rule has a tier. The CLI acts on one tier at a time (`--tier 1|2|3`) or on named packages (`--package`).

### Tier 1: Safe (default)
196 rules. Preloaded partner apps (Facebook, Microsoft Office apps, Netflix, Amazon), carrier apps, OEM ad services such as Xiaomi's MIUI System Ads (MSA Global, `com.miui.msa.global`), telemetry, and OEM extras such as Bixby, AR Emoji and AR Zone, game hubs and duplicate OEM cloud apps such as Xiaomi Cloud Backup. Suitable for most users to disable.

### Tier 2: Advanced
66 rules. Optional OEM and Google features that some people use: wallets and Samsung Pass, DeX, Link to Windows, theme stores and Galaxy Store, Android Auto, Digital Wellbeing, Modes and Routines, accessibility (TalkBack, Live Transcribe), OEM accounts and cloud (HeyTap Cloud), stock notes, recorder and file apps. Disable only if the feature is not used.

### Tier 3: Extreme
1 rule: the Transsion OTA updater (`com.transsion.otaupdate`). Disabling it stops system updates until it is enabled again. Stock dialer, contacts, SMS, keyboards and launchers are Tier 4 (blocked), not Tier 3.

### Tier 4: Critical (blocked)
89 core packages listed in `cli/rules/critical-do-not-touch.json` (section 4). The engine and the bridge both check this list before any change and refuse these packages, whatever tier, flag or prompt is used.

| Tier | Name | Rules | Who it is for | Can be changed |
|------|------|-------|---------------|----------------|
| 1 | Safe | 196 | Most users | Yes |
| 2 | Advanced | 66 | Users who know they do not use the feature | Yes |
| 3 | Extreme | 1 | Only on explicit request | Yes |
| 4 | Critical | 89 | Nobody | No, refused by the engine and the bridge |

---

## 3. How changes are made and undone

All changes target one Android user (user 0 unless `--user N` is given):

- `pm disable-user --user 0 <pkg>`: disables the app. It stays installed but cannot run, so its background services stop.
- `pm uninstall -k --user 0 <pkg>`: removes the app for that user only. `-k` keeps the app's data and cache directories. The APK stays on the system image.
- `pm enable --user 0 <pkg>`: undoes a disable.
- `cmd package install-existing --user 0 <pkg>` (or `pm install-existing` on older Android): undoes a per-user uninstall.

Neither command touches shared storage (photos, downloads, documents) or the system partition. Because preinstalled apps stay on the system image, a factory reset also brings them back.

Android versions: the code has no Android version check. Wireless debugging (QR or pairing code) needs Android 11 or newer. QR pairing is available in the CLI (`--qr-pair`) and in the web app when it is connected through the local bridge.

---

## 4. The critical list (Tier 4)

Source: `cli/rules/critical-do-not-touch.json` (89 entries). At import time the engine loads `HARDCRITICAL_PACKAGES` from that file; an 8-package built-in fallback is used only if the file cannot be read. `RuleSet.load` reloads the critical set from the same file, so there is one source, not a union of two lists. `validate_rules.py` rejects any rule in another file whose package is on the critical list. The web app builds its blocked set from the Tier 4 entries in `rules-dataset.json`.

All 89 packages:
- Framework: `android`, `com.android.server`, `com.android.server.account`, `com.android.server.activitymanager`, `com.android.server.appops`, `com.android.server.audio`, `com.android.server.backup`, `com.android.server.bluetooth`, `com.android.server.display`, `com.android.server.input`, `com.android.server.location`, `com.android.server.nfc`, `com.android.server.pm`, `com.android.server.power`, `com.android.server.telecom`, `com.android.server.telephony`, `com.android.server.wifi`
- System UI, settings, security and storage: `com.android.systemui`, `com.android.systemui.navbar`, `com.android.settings`, `com.android.providers.settings`, `com.android.keyguard`, `com.android.locksettings`, `com.android.biometrics`, `com.android.fingerprint`, `com.android.keychain`, `com.android.packageinstaller`, `com.android.shell`, `com.android.documentsui`, `com.android.externalstorage`, `com.android.providers.media`, `com.android.providers.downloads`, `com.android.sharedstoragebackup`, `com.android.mediacaserver`, `com.android.onetimeinitializer`, `com.android.partnercustomization`, `com.android.inputdevices`, `com.android.location`, `com.android.twilight`, `com.android.systemupdate`
- Phone, messaging and network: `com.android.phone`, `com.android.telephony`, `com.android.providers.telephony`, `com.android.dialer`, `com.android.incallui`, `com.android.contacts`, `com.android.providers.contacts`, `com.android.messaging`, `com.android.smspush`, `com.android.cellbroadcastreceiver`, `com.android.emergency`, `com.android.stk`, `com.android.ims`, `com.android.ims.rcsservice`, `com.android.carrierconfig`, `com.android.networkstack`, `com.android.ipsec`, `com.android.vpn`, `com.android.wifi`, `com.android.wifi.service`, `com.android.bluetooth`, `com.android.nfc`
- Stock apps and services: `com.android.launcher`, `com.android.launcher3`, `com.android.keyboard`, `com.android.providers.userdictionary`, `com.android.calendar`, `com.android.providers.calendar`, `com.android.desktopclock`, `com.android.browser`, `com.android.webview`, `com.android.wallpaper`, `com.android.printspooler`, `com.android.bips`, `com.android.vending`, `com.android.vending.licensing`
- Google: `com.google.android.gms`, `com.google.android.gms.auth`, `com.google.android.gms.account`, `com.google.android.gsf`, `com.google.android.ext.services`, `com.google.android.inputmethod.latin`, `com.google.android.webview`
- Samsung: `com.samsung.android.app.rss`, `com.samsung.android.app.samsungshare`, `com.samsung.android.app.sbrowser`, `com.samsung.android.mdxservice`, `com.samsung.android.oneconnect`, `com.samsung.android.scloud`

## 5. Rules per brand

`cli/rules/` has 10 files: 263 actionable rules plus 89 critical entries, 352 in total. The engine loads the critical file, then the universal file, then the files whose name or `manufacturer` field matches the connected phone (all brand files if the manufacturer is unknown).

| File | Brand | Rules | Tier 1 / 2 / 3 |
|------|-------|-------|----------------|
| `universal-safe-to-remove.json` | Universal (all brands) | 81 | 80 / 1 / 0 |
| `samsung-oneui.json` | Samsung | 44 | 25 / 19 / 0 |
| `xiaomi-miui-hyperos.json` | Xiaomi, Redmi, POCO | 27 | 26 / 1 / 0 |
| `google-pixel.json` | Google Pixel | 23 | 6 / 17 / 0 |
| `oneplus-oxygenos.json` | OnePlus | 19 | 16 / 3 / 0 |
| `bbk-oppo-vivo-realme.json` | Oppo, Vivo, Realme | 21 | 17 / 4 / 0 |
| `huawei-emui.json` | Huawei | 4 | 0 / 4 / 0 |
| `motorola.json` | Motorola | 15 | 11 / 4 / 0 |
| `transsion-tecno-infinix.json` | Transsion (Tecno, Infinix, itel) | 29 | 15 / 13 / 1 |
| `critical-do-not-touch.json` | Core system (Tier 4) | 89 | blocked |

Examples by brand (rule names as they appear in the rule files):
- Universal: Meta App Manager, Meta App Installer, Facebook, Microsoft OneDrive, Link to Windows Service, Netflix Partner Activation, Google Partner Setup, and carrier apps from AT&T, Verizon, T-Mobile, Sprint, Vodafone, Jio and Airtel.
- Samsung: Bixby Voice Agent, AR Zone, Game Optimizing Service (GOS), Knox Analytics Uploader, Samsung Free / Samsung News, Link to Windows (Phone Link), Samsung Quick Share Media Server, Galaxy Store.
- Xiaomi: MIUI System Ads (MSA Global), Joyose Performance Service, MIUI Analytics, Mi Pay, GetApps (Mi Picks), Mi Browser Global, Quick Apps, Xiaomi Cloud Backup.
- Google Pixel: Pixel Tips, Pixel Ambient Services (Now Playing), Device Health Services, Google Wallet (Quick Access Wallet), Digital Wellbeing, Android Auto, Live Transcribe.
- OnePlus: HeyTap Cloud, OPBugreport Lite, Red Cable Club (Membership), OnePlus LogKit, OnePlus Diagnostics, OnePlus Store, Zen Mode.
- Oppo, Vivo, Realme: Smart Assistant (Breeno Feed), ColorOS Game Space, HeyTap Browser, Oppo / Realme App Market, Vivo V-Appstore, Jovi Voice Assistant, Vivo Lockscreen Poster, iTheme (Vivo Themes).
- Huawei: Huawei System App Controller, Huawei AllShare, Huawei Push Service, Huawei AI Voice Assistant.
- Motorola: Moto Display (Peek Display), Moto Actions (Gestures), Moto Care Telemetry, Moto Gametime, Hello You (Moto Discover), Moto Device Help.
- Transsion: Palm Store (Transsion Phone Store), Carlcare, AHA Games, Phone Master / Security, Transsion Ads Framework, Transsion Telemetry, Transsion OTA Update (the only Tier 3 rule).

The full searchable list is at https://debloater.rovoxia.com/oems.

---

## 6. CLI commands (`cli/src/debloat_engine.py`)

Python 3.11+, standard library only.

- Interactive menu (default with no arguments): `python cli/src/debloat_engine.py --interactive`
- Scan and classify installed packages: `python cli/src/debloat_engine.py --scan` (add `--export-json [PATH]` to save the result)
- Dry run: `python cli/src/debloat_engine.py --tier 1 --dry-run`
- Apply a tier: `python cli/src/debloat_engine.py --tier 1 --action disable`
- Named packages only: `python cli/src/debloat_engine.py --package com.facebook.katana --dry-run` (repeatable; with `--tier`, only if the package is in that tier; critical packages are refused with a non-zero exit; a package with no rule is allowed with a warning and uses `--action`)
- `--action disable|uninstall` (default `disable`) applies to `--tier` or `--package`
- `--yes` skips the confirmation prompt; it is required for `--tier` or `--package` when there is no terminal
- `--no-backup` skips the restore snapshot
- Other Android user: `--user N` (default 0). Snapshots record the user; `--restore` uses the user stored in the snapshot
- Device selection: `--serial SERIAL`, `--adb-path PATH`, `--manufacturer NAME` (force a brand's rules)
- Wireless: `--wireless IP:PORT`, `--qr-pair` (Android 11+ QR pairing), `--switch-transport usb|wireless`, `--diagnostics`
- List snapshots: `python cli/src/debloat_engine.py --list-snapshots` (newest first, no phone needed)
- Restore the newest snapshot of the connected phone: `python cli/src/debloat_engine.py --restore`
- Restore a specific snapshot: `python cli/src/debloat_engine.py --restore ~/AiPhoneDebloater/backups/snapshot_<model>_<timestamp>.json` (file name, path or unique part of the name)
- Local web app bridge: `python cli/src/debloat_engine.py --bridge [--port 53123] [--allow-origin http://localhost:4321]` (`--allow-origin` is repeatable)
- Version: `python cli/src/debloat_engine.py --version` (read from the root `VERSION` file)
- Help: `python cli/src/debloat_engine.py --help`
- Rule validation: `python cli/tests/validate_rules.py`
- Unit tests: `python -m unittest discover -s cli/tests`

The plan and the confirmation list show the app name beside each package id.

Launchers (accept the same flags; no arguments opens the interactive menu):
- Windows: `cli\bin\debloat.bat`
- macOS and Linux: `bash cli/bin/debloat.sh`

Snapshots are written to `~/AiPhoneDebloater/backups/`. `cli/backups/` (repository) and `~/.ai-phone-debloater/backups/` (one-line install) are older locations that are still searched when restoring; nothing new is written there.

### Local bridge
`cli/src/bridge_server.py` (also started by `--bridge`) listens on `127.0.0.1:53123`. Every request must have a loopback `Host`, an allowlisted web origin and, on every route except `GET /health`, a per-session token in the `X-Bridge-Token` header (otherwise `401`). The bridge enforces the critical list but not tiers. The one-click scripts (`bridge.sh` and `bridge.ps1`) generate a random token per run, pass it in `AIPD_BRIDGE_TOKEN`, and open `https://debloater.rovoxia.com/app?bridge=1#token=<token>`; the fragment is not sent to servers, and the web app moves the token to `sessionStorage` and removes it from the address bar. A bridge started by hand prints that URL; paste it if the web app asks for a token, and treat it as a password for the session. A custom `AIPD_BRIDGE_TOKEN` must be at least 16 characters from `A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ ~ -`. Direct callers: `curl -H "X-Bridge-Token: <token>" http://127.0.0.1:53123/devices`.

### Web app (`/app`)
Connects over WebUSB (Chromium browsers) or the local bridge (any browser; `/app?bridge=1` connects automatically). Every change, batch or single package, opens a confirmation dialog that lists each package with its app name, and runs only after it is confirmed. The web app has no dry-run mode; dry run is a CLI feature (`--dry-run`). Snapshots are kept in the browser and can be exported as JSON. "Export CSV" downloads the currently filtered package list.

---

## 7. One-line install (no git)

- Windows (PowerShell): `irm https://debloater.rovoxia.com/run.ps1 | iex`
- macOS and Linux (Bash): `curl -fsSL https://debloater.rovoxia.com/run.sh | bash`
- Bridge for the web app: `https://debloater.rovoxia.com/bridge.ps1` and `https://debloater.rovoxia.com/bridge.sh`

The scripts download the `main` branch archive from GitHub and copy `cli/` and `VERSION` into `~/.ai-phone-debloater`. They compare the installed `VERSION` with the downloaded one and delete the bundled `tools/` (ADB platform-tools) only when the version changes, so fresh ADB binaries are fetched.

Source routes: `web/src/pages/run.ps1.ts`, `run.sh.ts`, `bridge.ps1.ts`, `bridge.sh.ts`; the prompt is served by `web/src/pages/prompt.md.ts`.

---

## 8. Rollback

1. Before each change the CLI and the bridge write a timestamped JSON snapshot of the affected packages' state to `~/AiPhoneDebloater/backups/snapshot_<model>_<timestamp>.json`. If the snapshot fails, nothing is changed. The web app over WebUSB keeps its snapshots in the browser.
2. Restore with the engine: `python cli/src/debloat_engine.py --restore <snapshot.json>`, or `--restore` with no value for the newest snapshot of the connected phone (`--list-snapshots` lists them).
3. Restore one app by hand: `adb shell cmd package install-existing --user 0 <pkg>` (after an uninstall) or `adb shell pm enable --user 0 <pkg>` (after a disable).
4. A factory reset also brings back every preinstalled app, because the APKs stay on the system image.

---

## 9. Master AI prompt

The master prompt lives at `prompt/master-prompt.md` and is served at https://debloater.rovoxia.com/prompt.md. An AI coding agent that can run commands (Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Cline, Aider, Codex and similar) or a chat assistant without a shell follows it in five steps:

1. Set up and connect over USB or wireless debugging.
2. Scan installed packages and classify them with `cli/rules/*.json`.
3. Plan and dry run (`--tier 1 --dry-run`, or `--package ... --dry-run` for a chosen subset), then show the plan.
4. Apply only after the user replies `PROCEED`, running the same command without `--dry-run` and with `--yes`.
5. Verify and hand over, including how to undo each change.

The prompt also has a raw ADB mode for when the engine cannot be used, with a manual snapshot before any change. Tier 3 is used only on explicit request, and critical packages are refused.

---

## 10. Repository layout

- `cli/src/debloat_engine.py`: CLI entry point and rule engine
- `cli/src/connection/`: device layer (USB, wireless, QR pairing, discovery, diagnostics)
- `cli/src/bridge_server.py`: local HTTP bridge for the web app (standalone)
- `cli/rules/*.json`: rule files (source of truth)
- `cli/tests/`: `validate_rules.py` and unit tests for the engine, connection layer, bridge and version sync; CI runs `python -m unittest discover -s cli/tests`
- `cli/generate_rules_dataset.py`: regenerates `web/src/data/rules-dataset.json` from `cli/rules/*.json`; CI fails if the committed file is out of date
- `cli/sync_version.py`: copies the root `VERSION` into the derived version fields
- `web/src/pages/index.astro`: home page
- `web/src/pages/app.astro` and `web/src/lib/webadb.ts`: web app (WebUSB and bridge clients)
- `web/src/pages/oems.astro`: searchable rule list
- `web/src/pages/blog.astro` and `web/src/pages/blog/[slug].astro`: blog index and guides
- `web/src/pages/404.astro`: not-found page
- `web/src/pages/run.ps1.ts`, `run.sh.ts`, `bridge.ps1.ts`, `bridge.sh.ts`, `prompt.md.ts`: script and prompt endpoints
- `web/src/data/rules-dataset.json`: generated copy of all 352 rules for the site
- `web/public/og-image.svg`, `og-image.png`, `og-image.jpg`: 1200x630 social card
- `web/public/robots.txt`, `llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt`, `pricing.md`: machine-readable files
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: CI (lint, rule validation, tests, web build and smoke test, security checks)
- `.github/workflows/release.yml`: creates GitHub Release `v<VERSION>` when a push to `main` changes `VERSION`, or on manual dispatch
- Root `VERSION`: the single source of the version number

---

## 11. Frequently asked questions

### What is AI Phone Debloater?
AI Phone Debloater is a free, open-source (MIT) tool that removes preinstalled Android apps over ADB without root. It checks each package against 352 curated rules in four safety tiers, refuses to touch 89 critical system packages, and writes a restore snapshot before each change. It runs as a Python CLI or as a web app at https://debloater.rovoxia.com/app.

### Do I need root to debloat my phone?
No. AI Phone Debloater uses standard ADB commands (`pm disable-user --user 0` and `pm uninstall -k --user 0`) that work with USB debugging on a stock phone. It does not root the phone, unlock the bootloader or write to the system partition.

### Does debloating void the warranty or trip Samsung Knox?
AI Phone Debloater does not root the phone, unlock the bootloader, flash anything or write to the system partition. It only disables or removes apps for one user through ADB. Whether that matters for Knox or for a warranty is for the manufacturer and the seller to say, so this project cannot promise how they treat a debloated phone.

### Do banking apps and Google Pay keep working?
The tool does not root the phone, unlock the bootloader or install anything such as Magisk. This project does not test Play Integrity results or individual banking apps, so it makes no promise about them. An app that depends on a package you disabled can stop working; if that happens, restore the package from the snapshot. Google Play services (`com.google.android.gms`) is on the critical list, so the tool refuses to disable it.

### Will debloating affect OTA system updates?
No, with one exception. It operates in user 0 without touching read-only system partitions, so official OTA updates install normally. The exception is the single Tier 3 rule, the Transsion OTA updater (`com.transsion.otaupdate`): disabling it stops system updates until you enable it again.

### Can critical Android packages be removed by mistake?
The engine and the bridge check every package against the 89-entry critical list (System UI, telephony, package installer, settings, Google Play services, the stock dialer, contacts, SMS, keyboards, launchers and others) and refuse to disable or uninstall them, whatever tier, flag or prompt is used. Other packages can still break a feature you rely on, which is why every change can be undone from its snapshot.

### Will my phone be faster or the battery last longer?
Disabling preinstalled apps stops their background services, which frees memory and reduces background battery and data use. The gain depends on the phone and on what was running; this project does not publish measurements.

### Does it delete my data?
No user files are touched. `pm disable-user` keeps the app and its data. `pm uninstall -k` removes the app for one user but keeps its data and cache directories, so a restored app comes back with its data. Shared storage such as photos and downloads is not affected by either command.

### Which Android versions work?
The code has no Android version check, and this project does not publish a list of tested versions. It needs USB debugging; wireless debugging and QR pairing need Android 11 or newer.

### Does the web app have a dry run?
No. Dry run is a CLI flag (`--dry-run`). The web app shows a confirmation dialog listing every package before each change.

### What does it cost?
Nothing. It is MIT-licensed, with no paid edition, ads, telemetry or account. See https://debloater.rovoxia.com/pricing.md.
